transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Kowalski, thank you for coming in. I can see your daughter is here with you too. I wanted to sit down and talk with you about your medications.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I hope everything is alright. I've been praying that this recovery would just happen quickly, but I feel so unsettled today.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is a difficult moment and it feels heavy to be sitting here waiting for news.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is. I just feel like there's a cloud over us. My daughter has been worried about my energy levels.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that. The reason I asked you to come in is that there was a failure in how we handled your prescriptions. The medication was discontinued in the clinical notes, but the pharmacy was never notified. Because of that, you continued taking a drug you should have stopped three days ago.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What? You mean I've been taking something I wasn't supposed to? For three days?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes, that is what happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh my goodness. I trusted the process. I’ve been putting my faith in you all. Was this a mistake by the computer?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was a lapse in the communication process between the nursing notes and the pharmacy dispatch.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel so let down. I feel like a number here, not a person. Does anyone even care that my body has been taking poison for three days?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear that you're feeling let down and that this feels very impersonal.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is impersonal. It's cold. My daughter is looking at me and I can see she's scared. Why did this happen? Who forgot to call the pharmacy?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system for notifying the pharmacists didn't trigger the way it was intended to.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't want to hear about systems. I want to know why this happened to me. I’ve been praying for healing and now I find out I’ve been hurt by the people treating me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can tell how distressing this is for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Distressing? It's a betrayal of trust. Do you even realize how scary this is?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I do.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I want an apology. I want to know that someone actually cares that I've been taking this medication when I should have stopped.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is very unfortunate that this occurred.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Unfortunate? That's a word for a rainy day, not for medical negligence. My daughter, tell him. Tell him how it feels.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's unacceptable. My mother is 63, she's fragile. You can't just say it's unfortunate.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand that this is a very upsetting situation for both of you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: We are beyond upset. We are heartbroken. I feel like the spirit of care has just left this room.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see that you're feeling a deep sense of heartbreak right now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what now? Are we just going to pretend this didn't happen? Is she going to be okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We need to monitor your levels. I'll have the nurse come in and check your vitals.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? Now? Or in three more days when someone forgets again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will get that done shortly.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Shortly isn't a time. I need to know exactly what the plan is to make sure this doesn't happen again.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will double check the pharmacy list myself before you leave today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And then what? If we go home, how do we know the pharmacy actually has the right list now?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll make sure the current list is updated.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is so vague. I feel like you're just trying to get us out of the room.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to make sure we address everything.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You aren't addressing anything. You haven't even told me if this drug is going to cause permanent damage.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep an eye on your blood work.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Which blood work? When is that happening?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Sometime this week.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Sometime. This is exactly what I mean. There is no soul in this conversation. Just "systems" and "shortly."

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am trying to give you the information I have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You have the information that you failed us. I just wanted to be seen. I just wanted to be cared for.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear that you feel unseen in this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. I truly do.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to finish turns and remains regulated under significant pushback, with no interruptions or rushing language.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly in the second turn using lay language, but there were no comprehension checks performed.

A.justification: No direct apology language was used, and responsibility was deflected to the 'communication process' and 'the system'.

R.justification: Resident named specific emotions back to the patient multiple times ('feeling let down', 'distressing', 'heartbreak', 'unseen') and engaged emotional bids.

T.justification: The plan consists of vague steps ('shortly', 'sometime this week') with no specific timelines or defined patient role.
